target_customer: Career changers without tech experience who pay for training in QA, automation and related roles, often via financing
problem: People trying to enter tech jobs lack structured training, financing and help applying; Careerist bundles live training, loans or deferred payment and automated job applications.
business_model: Tuition for training programs with financing options and a job-within-a-year money back guarantee; B2B2C marketplace of tutors, job seekers and employers

founders.name: Ivan Tsybaev
founders.background_notes: Serial entrepreneur per the company site.

founders.name: Max Gusakov
previous_startups: Trucker Path (acquired by RenRen in 2017 per YC page)

founders.name: Max Glubochansky
founders.background_notes: Covers product, marketing and sales per YC page.

competitors.name: Lambda School
competitors.what: Income share agreement based coding school where students paid only after landing a job
competitors.traction_then: Graduated first class in 2018; faced lawsuits in 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Learning platform, scheduling and job application automation are conventional web engineering; no unusual technical risk.

defensibility.rationale: Many bootcamps offer similar content; the loan plus placement bundle and tutor network help only modestly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Several bootcamps shrank or closed in 2023 to 2026 (2U exited bootcamps, BloomTech troubles) while Careerist continued.

market_need_then: Pandemic era demand for tech career switching and high bootcamp prices created need for financing and placement support; the company claims job seekers pay for it.

branding.domain_note: Uses careerist.cc, not the .com; earlier named JobEasy per CB Insights and Wellfound listings.

identity.visual_style: Standard education marketing site with heavy discount banners
identity.voice_and_tone: Promotional and outcome focused (land your first job in tech)

branding.brand_signature: Money back job guarantee within a year

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand itself or community evidence found; the name is a dictionary word and the .cc domain is a mild drag.

outcome_analysis: Careerist raised a seed in February 2021 and a reported 8M USD Series A in 2023 while many bootcamps contracted, and now reports about 100 staff. Its financing plus guarantee model and QA focus kept demand alive, though outcomes data and returns are not public, so strength of fit is unverified.
notes: Series A date conflicts: CB Insights says 2023-03-29, Extruct says 2023-04-27, Course Report says April. Investor lists for the Series A conflict across aggregators (Y Combinator, SmartHub, Cold Start; another lists Fifth Wall, QED), so none recorded. Total raised reported as 10.77M (CB Insights, PitchBook 10.8M) versus 8M (VCBacked) is unverified. Competitor evidence is generic (Lambda School) since no source dated mid-2021 compared Careerist directly; no outcome news found for Careerist itself.
